page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance featuring 2 vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM, translating to 4.0 GB of memory per core. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the instance utilizes a dedicated Intel processor with 1 physical core and 2 threads. The CPU cache configuration includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 260 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, and it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates moderate single-core capabilities alongside constrained multi-core and memory performance. The instance achieves average ratings in single-core metrics, such as a stress-ng single-core score of 1684.29 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1834.0. However, multi-core and memory subsystem benchmarks are notably limited. The stress-ng multi-core CPU score is 1714.68, and the Geekbench multi-core score is 2251.0, both falling into the poor to weak categories. Memory bandwidth is also restricted, with large-block read and write speeds measured at 19.35 GB/sec and 12.78 GB/sec, respectively.

Given its hardware profile and benchmark results, the n4-standard-2 is positioned as an entry-level option for lightweight workloads. It is suitable for basic web serving, simple text processing, and minor single-threaded tasks. It is less suited for memory-intensive databases, software compilation, or multi-threaded processing, as evidenced by its poor Passmark database operations score of 1259.2 and weak static web serving throughput of 4.0 GB/sec. From a cost-efficiency perspective, it offers a low-resource entry point for development and testing environments where high throughput and parallel processing are not required.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-2 is an entry-level, general-purpose virtual machine featuring 2 vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM on an x86_64 Intel architecture. Operating with 1 physical core and 2 threads, the instance includes a 260 MB L3 cache but lacks bundled local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks reveal a clear division between single-core and multi-core capabilities; single-core metrics like Geekbench (1834.0) and stress-ng (1684.29) perform at average levels, whereas multi-core and memory bandwidth tests show poor to weak results. For example, the Geekbench multi-core score is 2251.0, and large-block memory read bandwidth is limited to 19.35 GB/sec. Consequently, this instance is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded applications, basic text processing, and small-scale development or testing environments rather than demanding database operations or parallelized workloads.
